THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, OCTOBER 7, 1932

RETURN OF CARPETS
ORDERED
District Court Decision
In Case Brought
By Persian

A sequel to a case recently heard before the U. S. Court for China here has come before the First Special District Court which has just delivered judgment for Mr. D. Joukel, of the East West Export and Import Company, against Mr. J. Ogly, for the return of a quantity of Persian carpets. Mr. Joukel was represented by Dr. F. Wilhelm, of Messrs. Musso, Fischer and Wilhelm.

Mr. Joukel recently figured as plaintiff in an action in the U. S. Court for China against the Thriftcor Bank for the return of the carpets or their value, alleging that the carpets had been unlawfully mortgaged to the bank by a third party.

Plaintiff's Case

Dr. Wilhelm told the court that the East West Export and Import Company represented by plaintiff originally was established at Meshad, Persia. Owing to the extension of the company's business, counsel said, Mr. Rosenblum was sent to China to sell its merchandise. Plaintiff subsequently was appointed as representative of the company here. Before his arrival it was stated, the company had already shipped a number of carpets to China for delivery to Mr. Rosenblum. The carpets arrived in Harbin by train and were delivered to the Asiatic Transportation Company.

The greater part of the goods, it was stated, was sold by Messrs. Choorin and Company and the remainder was shipped to Shanghai via Dairen.

Defendant, it was stated, rented certain premises at 4, Ezra Road, for storage of carpets. When the lease on the premises terminated, it was stated, plaintiff agreed to allow defendant to look after the storage of a number of carpets. Out of 23 carpets it was alleged, only seven were subsequently returned to plaintiff.

Under the heading of statements by plaintiff and his counsel, the judgment of the court states: "In May, 1930, two months after plaintiff's arrival, two lots of carpets sent by the East West Export and Import Company of Persia amounting to 27 bales and another lot amounting to three bales had already arrived here from Meshad via Bombay and plaintiff had received the bills of lading from Meshad and had consulted with Mr. Rosenblum. That both of them thought the carpets could be sold in Dairen more easily than in Shanghai.

Bills Of Lading

Defendant not only knew English, but also was the salesman of the East West Export and Import Company and consequently the bills of lading, covering the 27 bales and three bales of carpets were delivered to him by plaintiff with instructions to ship the goods to Dairen & have them stored in the name of the East West Export and Import Company. That the bills of lading were endorsed by defendant proving that that he had received the goods.

Several days later defendant returned the bills of lading which plaintiff filed away, but could not find when plaintiff finally decided to ship the goods to London."

The judgment then referred to a separate criminal action taken by plaintiff against defendant during the trial of which it was stated, the defence was that Mr. Rosenblum owed defendant some money and that the latter had retained the goods as security for the loan.

Continuing the judgment stated: "It was alleged by plaintiff that counsel for defendant claimed that the 23 carpets were acquired through special circumstances, but could not prove them. That the bills of lading covering the 30 bales and various documents all bore the name of the East West Export and Import Company and therefore, that there was not the slightest doubt that the carpets were the property of plaintiff. That plaintiff had lost the bills of lading and the same were in the hands of defendant."

Shipment Of Goods

"That since defendant had pledged the bill of lading covering 27 bales of the goods to the Thriftcor Bank there was danger that the bill of lading covering the other three bales and another 16 bales would be disposed of by him and also that long storage might cause deterioration of the goods."

Reverting to the defence the judgment stated: "In connection with the 23 carpets, it was claimed that they were sent to Harbin by Rosenblum and delivered to defendant. That the remainder of the goods were shipped to Shanghai from Harbin."

《字林西报》，1932年10月7日，星期五

地毯归还令
地区法院判决
波斯人提起的诉讼案

此前在中国美国法院审理的一起案件的后续事宜已提交至第一特区地方法院，该院刚刚作出判决，支持东西进出口公司（East West Export and Import Company）的D. Joukel先生，裁定J. Ogly先生归还一批波斯地毯。Joukel先生由Musso, Fischer and Wilhelm律师事务所的F. Wilhelm博士代理。

Joukel先生最近作为原告，在中国美国法院对Thriftcor银行提起诉讼，要求归还地毯或赔偿其价值，指控这些地毯被第三方非法抵押给该银行。

原告方陈述

Wilhelm博士告诉法庭，由原告代表的东西进出口公司最初成立于波斯马什哈德（Meshad）。律师称，由于公司业务扩展，Rosenblum先生被派往中国销售其商品。随后，原告被任命为该公司在华代表。据称，在他抵达之前，公司已将一批地毯运往中国，交付给Rosenblum先生。地毯经火车运抵哈尔滨，并交付给亚洲运输公司（Asiatic Transportation Company）。

据称，大部分货物由Choorin公司出售，其余部分经大连运往上海。

据称，被告租赁了爱多亚路（Ezra Road）4号的某处房产用于存放地毯。据称，当该房产租约终止时，原告同意让被告代为保管一批地毯。据称，在23块地毯中，随后仅向原告归还了7块。

在原告及其律师的陈述标题下，法院判决书指出：“1930年5月，即原告抵达两个月后，由波斯东西进出口公司发出的两批地毯（共计27包）以及另一批（共计3包）已从马什哈德经孟买运抵此处，原告已收到来自马什哈德的提单，并与Rosenblum先生进行了商议。他们两人均认为地毯在大连比在上海更容易售出。”

提单

被告不仅懂英语，而且是东西进出口公司的推销员，因此，涵盖这27包和3包地毯的提单由原告交付给他，并指示他将货物运往大连，并以东西进出口公司的名义存储。被告在提单上背书，证明他已收到货物。

几天后，被告归还了提单，原告将其归档保存，但当原告最终决定将货物运往伦敦时，却找不到这些提单。”

判决书接着提到了原告在审判期间对被告提起的另一项刑事诉讼，其中辩称，Rosenblum先生欠被告一些钱，后者扣留货物作为贷款的担保。

判决书继续指出：“原告声称，被告律师声称这23块地毯是通过特殊情况获得的，但无法证明。涵盖30包地毯的提单和各种文件均印有东西进出口公司的名称，因此，毫无疑问，地毯是原告的财产。原告遗失了提单，而这些提单在被告手中。”

货物运输

“由于被告已将涵盖27包货物的提单质押给Thriftcor银行，存在他将处置涵盖另外3包及另16包货物的提单的危险，而且长期储存可能导致货物变质。”

回到辩护方面，判决书指出：“关于这23块地毯，据称它们是由Rosenblum运往哈尔滨并交付给被告的。其余货物从哈尔滨运往上海。”

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, SEPTEMBER 27, 1932

GODOWN WARRANT IN
DISPUTE

Illegal Hypothecation
Is Alleged By
A Persian

Illegal hypothecation of a go-
down warrant was alleged against
Mr. M. J. Ogly by Mr. D. Joukel,
a partner of the East West Ex-
port and Import Company, when
bringing an action before Judge
Milton D. Purdy, in the U. S. Court
for China yesterday, against the
Thriftcor Bank for the return of
the warrant or for its equivalent:
Kran 113,933.65 Persian money.
The case was adjourned.
The godown warrant was for 27
bales of Persian carpets. In his
complaint Mr. Joukel stated that
the East West Export and Import
Company was a co-partnership
with head office in Meshed, Persia.
In May, 1930, the complaint stated,
plaintiff arrived here and became
acquainted with Mr. Ogly through
a business associate. Not long
after, he said, his firm shipped to
him the 27 bales of carpets and
Mr. Ogly volunteered to assist him
in landing the goods and obtained
the documents from him. Instead
of executing the godown warrant
in favour of the East West Import
and Export Company, the complaint
continued, Mr. Ogly had it made
out in his own name and on May
24, "surreptitiously" secured the
godown warrant having access to
his office, and subsequently pledg-
ed the warrant as security to the
Thriftcor Bank against a personal
overdraft of Mr. Ogly. In due
course, it was stated, Mr. Ogly
withdrew various sums from the
bank amounting to $264.59 and
Tls. 2,215.88.
Mr. Joukel said he later asked
the bank for the return of the
warrant, offering to pay any sums
owing to the bank by Mr. Ogly,
but without avail.

（批：File under Ogly）

d.b. (crime)
Information.
J.P. Greeno
O. i/c Sp. Br.
SEP. 2 8 1932

《字林西报》，1932年9月27日，星期二

仓单争议

波斯人指控
非法抵押

东西进出口公司合伙人D. Joukel先生昨日在中国美国法院Milton D. Purdy法官面前对Thriftcor银行提起诉讼，要求归还仓单或等值金额：113,933.65克兰（Kran，波斯货币），指控M. J. Ogly先生非法抵押仓单。案件延期审理。
该仓单涉及27包波斯地毯。Joukel先生在诉状中指出，东西进出口公司是一家合伙企业，总部设在波斯马什哈德（Meshed）。诉状称，1930年5月，原告抵达此地，并通过一位商业伙伴结识了Ogly先生。他说，不久之后，他的公司向他在运了27包地毯，Ogly先生主动协助他卸货，并从他那里取得了文件。诉状继续称，Ogly先生没有开具以东西进出口公司为受益人的仓单，而是开成了他自己的名字，并于5月24日“偷偷”利用进入其办公室的机会获取了仓单，随后将该仓单作为Ogly先生个人透支的担保质押给Thriftcor银行。据称，随后Ogly先生从银行提取了总计264.59美元和2,215.88两银元的款项。
Joukel先生说，他后来要求银行归还仓单，并提出愿意支付Ogly先生欠银行的任何款项，但未果。

（批：归入Ogly档案）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
REPORT

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY No. S. B. D 1184 Section 2. Branch; date 17.11.31 Date November 17, 1931.）

Subject (in full) M.G. Ogly.

Made by D.S. Tcheremshansky. Forwarded by （签名）

With reference to the extract from the French Daily
Intelligence Report of November 7, 1931 on the subject of the above,
inquiries show that this individual appeared before the Shanghai
Special District Court on November 4, on a charge of misappropri-
ating a quantity of carpets to the value of approximately Tls.
30,000, the property of one Devouc Joukel, Persian, residing at
No.12 Chusan Road. The case was remanded for one week, Ogly
being ordered to be released on security failing which he would
be detained in custody. On November 10, the necessary security
was furnished by one George Hoper of American Mineral Sanitarium,
No.1205 Bubbling Well Road. At the hearing on November 11, the
case was remanded until November 18. The history and record
of M.G. Ogly as known to the Municipal Police are as follows.
M.G. Ogly, Persian, was formerly an important
member of the G.P.U. (State Political Police) in Vladivostok.
In 1920 he was attached to the Soviet Consulate in Harbin and
was employed as a secret courier operating between Harbin, Chita
and Habarovsk.
During January 1930, in company with one Z.Rosemblum,
a suspected agent of the G.P.U., he arrived in Shanghai. Shortly
afterwards they established at No.609 East Broadway, a trading
company under the name of "East West Export and Import Company".
At this address they carried on business as importers of valuable
Persian carpets and dried fruits until May 1931 when they removed
to No.4 Edward Ezra Road. Here they remained until September
1931, when the office was removed to No.65, Baikal Road, the
residence of Ogly.
The carpets, it is said, were supplied through the
Gostorg (Soviet Trade Mission) and had been confiscated by the

上海公共租界工部局警务处
报告

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 C. & S. B. 登记处 编号 S. B. D 1184 第2分部；日期 1931年11月17日 日期 1931年11月17日。）

主题（全称） M.G. Ogly。

由 D.S. Tcheremshansky 制作。由 （签名） 转呈

关于1931年11月7日法国每日情报报告中关于上述主题的摘录，调查显示，此人于11月4日出现在上海特区地方法院，被控侵占居住在中山路12号的波斯人Devouc Joukel所有的一批价值约30,000两银元的地毯。案件延期一周审理，命令Ogly提供保释金释放，否则将被拘留。11月10日，由泡灵井路（Bubbling Well Road）1205号美国矿泉疗养院（American Mineral Sanitarium）的George Hoper提供了必要的保释金。在11月11日的听证会上，案件延期至11月18日。工部局警务处所知的M.G. Ogly的历史和记录如下。
M.G. Ogly，波斯人，曾是符拉迪沃斯托克（海参崴）国家政治保卫局（G.P.U.，即国家政治警察）的重要成员。
1920年，他隶属于苏联驻哈尔滨领事馆，并被雇用为在哈尔滨、赤塔（Chita）和哈巴罗夫斯克（Habarovsk）之间活动的秘密信使。
1930年1月，他与疑似G.P.U.特工Z.Rosemblum一同抵达上海。不久之后，他们在百老汇路（East Broadway）609号成立了一家名为“东西进出口公司”的贸易公司。
在此地址，他们从事贵重波斯地毯和干果的进口业务，直到1931年5月搬至爱多亚路（Edward Ezra Road）4号。他们在此停留至1931年9月，随后办公室迁至贝加尔路（Baikal Road）65号，即Ogly的住所。
据说，这些地毯是通过苏联贸易代表团（Gostorg）供应的，并已被

On October 13, Ogly was arrested at his home by the
Shanghai Judicial Police on the authority of a despatch issued
by the Harbin Court, on a charge of having failed to pay the
sum of Yen 1,000, adjudged to one Professor Engelfeld, resident
of Harbin, as the outcome of same civil dispute. Ogly appeared
before the Execution Court on the same date and tendered $206
in cash together with a cheque on a certain local bank for the
balance, to Mr. M.E. Gilcher, Russian lawyer, the legal
representative of Professor Engelfeld. It is reported that
when the cheque was presented it was returned owing to
insufficiency of funds.
A cursory examination of the documents found in the
possession Ogly, made by the Judicial Police disclosed that he
had certain business connections with Soviet officials and
concerns and that when he communicated with addresses in Harbin,
he sent his messages in code. It was also ascertained that he
had made several trips to South China.
Attached herewith is a copy of the original
complaint lodged on October 10, 1931, by L. Joukel against Ogly
at Wayside Station who referred him to the Shanghai Special Dis-
trict Court for civil action, together with a cutting from the
North China Daily News of November 5, concerning this case.
Further information regarding the activities of
Ogly is contained in the file no. D.1184.

10月13日，Ogly在其家中被上海司法警察逮捕，依据是哈尔滨法院发出的一份公函，指控他未支付因同一民事纠纷判给哈尔滨居民Engelfeld教授的1,000日元。Ogly于同日出庭执行法院，向Engelfeld教授的法律代表、俄罗斯律师M.E. Gilcher先生支付了206美元现金，并就余额开具了一张当地某银行的支票。据报道，当该支票提示付款时，因资金不足被退回。
司法警察对Ogly身上携带的文件进行的粗略检查显示，他与苏联官员和企业有某些业务联系，并且当他与哈尔滨的地址通信时，使用密码发送信息。还查明他曾多次前往华南地区。
随附的是L. Joukel于1931年10月10日在韦斯特赛德分局（Wayside Station）对Ogly提出的原始投诉副本，该局将他转介至上海特区地方法院进行民事诉讼，以及11月5日《华北每日新闻》关于此案的剪报。
关于Ogly活动的进一步信息包含在档案号D.1184中。

Copy
The Shanghai Municipal Police.
Petitioner: Persian Subject Davoud Doukel
residing 12 Chusan Road Room 2, Shanghai.
My brother, with another Persian subject and myself formed
a partnership named The East Export & Import Co. in Meshed,
Persia.
It was intented that Messers Rosenblum, Sherel and a
Persian by the name Ogly, all resident in China should be the
other partners in the Co. They were to contribute a certain
proportion of the capital.
But no one of them paid any money.
In May the Head Office in Persia Forwarded to Shanghai
30 packages of Persian carpets of the value of Taels 30000,
total 107 carpets, and these were addressed in my name.
The carpets arrived in Shanghai in July 1930. As our
firm had a Branch in Shanghai and Ogly was working in this
Branch I endorsed the Bills of Lading and asked Ogly to
receive the carpets and to ship them to Dairen, where I
intended to sell them. This transaction was made through
the Chinese Eastern Railway.
Ogly stored the carpets in Dairen with the Chinese
Eastern Rwy Agency but stored them not in the name of our
Company but in his own name.
I ask Ogly many times to deliver the carpets to the Co,
of which I am the sole representative in China acting under
a power of attorney issued in Meshed. I intended to ship
the carpets to London. But Ogly refused to return the
carpets to the Co.
In the mean time I received information that Ogly had
mortgaged to the Thriftcor Bank Shanghai 8-c-a Kiukiang Road,
the documents of the carpets stored in Dairen.
page_data.zh:
副本
上海公共租界工部局警务处。
申请人：波斯籍臣民 Davoud Doukel，
住址：上海中山路12号2室。
我的兄弟、另一位波斯籍臣民以及我本人，在波斯马什哈德（Meshed）组建了一家名为“东方进出口公司”（The East Export & Import Co.）的合伙企业。
原计划由居住在中国的 Rosenblum 先生、Sherel 先生以及一位名为 Ogly 的波斯人作为公司的其他合伙人。他们需出资一定比例的资本。
但他们均未支付任何款项。
五月，位于波斯的总公司向上海发运了30包波斯地毯，价值关平银30,000两，共计107条地毯，这些货物是以我的名义托运的。
地毯于1930年7月抵达上海。由于我司在上海设有分公司，且 Ogly 在该分公司工作，我便背书了提单，并要求 Ogly 接收地毯并将其运往大连，我打算在那里出售这批货物。这笔交易是通过中东铁路（Chinese Eastern Railway）进行的。
Ogly 将地毯存放在大连的中东铁路代理处，但并非以我们公司的名义存放，而是以他个人的名义存放。
我多次要求 Ogly 将地毯交付给公司，我是该公司在中国的唯一代表，持有在马什哈德签发的授权委托书。我原计划将地毯运往伦敦。但 Ogly 拒绝将地毯归还给公司。
与此同时，我获悉 Ogly 已将存于大连的地毯单据抵押给了位于九江路8-c-a号的上海节俭银行（Thriftcor Bank）。

page_data.en:
(2)

In addition to refusing to deliver the above mentioned
carpets Ogly misappropriated 23 Persian carpets belonging
to the same Co. and which had remained unsold in Shanghai.
He reported that they were at Mr. Ezra's on approval but
the latter denied it and said that they had been taken
back by Mr. Ogly. I have reason to suppose that some of
the carpets are stored at 85 Baikal Road, in the residence
of Mr. Ogly.

Mr. Ogly also was unable to account for saffron and
ginsen belonging to the Co.

Mr. Ogly seized all bills and documents belonging to
the Co. and refused to restore them.

I am asking the Shanghai Municipal Police to make an
urgent investigation of the matter and have the evidence
of Mr. Salmon Rosenblum, whose residence is 12 Chusan Road
Room 1.

I am also asking for the arrest of Mr. Ogly, who is in
hiding, for the seizure of the goods and documents belonging
to the Co.

I ask further that Mr. Ogly be brought before the
Criminal Court for misappropriation and theft of documents.

(Signed) L. Joukel.
(Dated) October 10, 1931
Shanghai.
page_data.zh:
(2)

除了拒绝交付上述地毯外，Ogly 还侵占了属于同一公司的23条波斯地毯，这些地毯此前一直未在上海售出。
他声称这些地毯正放在 Ezra 先生处供其审阅，但后者予以否认，并称这些地毯已被 Ogly 先生取回。我有理由推测，部分地毯存放在白克路85号 Ogly 先生的住所内。

Ogly 先生也无法说明属于公司的藏红花和人参的下落。

Ogly 先生扣押了属于公司的所有账单和文件，并拒绝归还。

我请求上海公共租界工部局警务处对此事进行紧急调查，并传唤居住在中山路12号1室的 Salmon Rosenblum 先生作证。

我还请求逮捕正在躲藏的 Ogly 先生，并查封属于公司的货物和文件。

我进一步请求将 Ogly 先生移送刑事法庭，以其侵占及盗窃文件罪受审。

（签名）L. Joukel。
（日期）1931年10月10日
上海。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, NOVEMBER 5, 1931

PERSIAN SUBJECT
IN COURT

Alleged Misappropriation
of Carpets

Charged with misappropriating
goods valued at approximately Tls.
40,000 belonging to Mr. D. J. Joukel,
of the East-West Import & Export
Co., M. J. Ogly, a Persian, was ar-
raigned before Judge Shen in the
Special District Court yesterday.
The case was remanded for a week,
accused being ordered to be held by
Police unless he was able to put
up a guarantee for his presence in
Court whenever required.
Complainant, represented by Dr.
F. Wilhelm, of Messrs. Musso, Fis-
cher & Wilhelm, told the Court that
he represented the East-West Im-
port & Export Co. and arrived in
Shanghai in May, 1930. Two months
after his arrival here, he received
from Persia documents (bills of
lading, invoices, etc.) covering a
shipment of 30 bales of carpets for
the China market. Being for the
first time in China and unfamiliar
with conditions here, he was advised
by accused not to import carpets to
Shanghai on the ground that heavy
customs duty would be payable, but
to forward the whole shipment to
Dairen where the goods could be
stored in godowns.
He took accused's advice and
handed over the shipping documents
to accused who then shipped the
goods to Dairen, but, instead of de-
positing the goods in the name of
the complainant, or the East-West
Import & Export Co., as he had been
instructed to do so, he deposited the
goods in his own name, a fact which
became known to complainant when
he intended to ship the goods to
London. He further discovered that
accused not only had stored the
goods in his own name, but had
pledged the godown warrant cover-
ing 27 of the 30 bales of carpets
with an American bank in Shanghai
for the sum of $2,000, and when
he was requested to return the
godown war- nt, etc., to the com-
plainant, he refused to do so.
Accused, the complainant told the
Court, also kept in his possession
23 carpets, which were also com-
plainant's goods, and he had dis-
posed of part of the goods and kept
the proceeds of sale. As accused
had taken unlawful possession of
documents and papers not belonging
to him and refused to return the
same to their owner, the Court was
requested to deal with accused ac-
cording to law and to refuse bail for
him because it was feared that he
would abscond from Shanghai in the
event of his being bailed out, stated
complainant.
Questioned by the Court, accused
denied the charge and stated that
the 30 bales of carpets in question
had been pledged with him by a
foreigner who owed him a consider-
able sum of money.

《字林西报》，1931年11月5日，星期四

波斯籍臣民
出庭受审

涉嫌侵占
地毯案

M. J. Ogly，一名波斯人，被控侵占属于“东西进出口公司”（East-West Import & Export Co.）D. J. Joukel 先生、价值约关平银40,000两的货物，昨日在特区法院由沈法官提审。
本案延期一周审理，被告被命令由警方羁押，除非他能提供担保，保证在法院需要时随时到庭。
原告由 Musso, Fischer & Wilhelm 律师事务所的 F. Wilhelm 博士代理，向原告庭陈述称，他代表东西进出口公司，于1930年5月抵达上海。抵沪两个月后，他收到来自波斯的文件（提单、发票等），涉及一批运往中国市场的30包地毯。由于是初次来华，不熟悉当地情况，被告建议他不要将地毯进口到上海，理由是需缴纳高额关税，而应将整批货物发往大连，以便将货物存入仓库。
他采纳了被告的建议，并将运输单据交给被告，被告随即将货物运往大连，但是，被告未按指示以原告或东西进出口公司的名义存放货物，而是以个人名义存放，这一事实是在原告打算将货物运往伦敦时才得知的。他还发现，被告不仅以个人名义存放货物，还将涵盖30包地毯中27包的仓单抵押给了上海的一家美国银行，借款金额为2,000美元，当原告要求被告归还仓单等文件时，被告拒绝照办。
原告告诉法庭，被告还占有了23条地毯，这些也是原告的货物，被告已处置了部分货物并私吞了销售所得。鉴于被告非法占有不属于他的文件和纸张，并拒绝将其归还原主，原告请求法庭依法处置被告，并拒绝其保释，因为担心被告若获保释会从上海潜逃。
经法庭讯问，被告否认指控，并称涉案的30包地毯是一名欠他巨额款项的外国人抵押给他的。

Para.5. M. OGLY ARRESTED FOR FRAUD.

We are informed that M. Ogly an auxiliary agent
of the G.P.U., and "proprietor" of the "China Persia
Co." (No.4 Ezra Road) dealing in carpets exported from
the USSR, was arrested for fraud on November 3rd and is
at present detained at the Central Police Station of
the International Settlement.

1931年11月7日法国警察每日情报报告摘录译文

第5段. M. OGLY 因欺诈被捕。

据闻，M. Ogly 系国家政治保卫局（G.P.U.）的辅助特工，亦是经营从苏联出口地毯的“中国波斯公司”（China Persia Co.，地址：爱多亚路4号）的“老板”，他于11月3日因欺诈罪被捕，目前被拘押在国际租界中央巡捕房。
